title: windowing-heuristic-telltales
content:
One-line summary:
Observed intermittent 20-60% throughput drops for mixed short+long workloads after the recent windowing heuristic toggle (rollout 2025-01-08). Symptoms point to alignment mismatches between the request time-slicing and the continuous-batcher warmup path, causing underfilled windows + increased per-token overhead.

Why I care:
- Customer impact: tail latency spikes and lower token throughput for apps with many short requests interleaved with occasional long ones (chat logs).
- Rollout PR touched window_size_estimator and the fixed-alignment fallback. Might be an edge-case regression in the estimator when sequence_length variance high.

Observed signals (metrics + qualitative):
- Serving throughput (tokens/s) drops ~25% on average for the affected stacks during 09:00-11:00 PST window on Jan 9 and Jan 13.
- Queue depth metric shows more frequent small batches (1-4 requests) instead of expected medium batches (8-32).
- KV-cache hit-rate decreased by ~12% correlated with drop periods.
- CPU utilization on GPU hosts unchanged; latency per token increased ~6-12%.

Timeline (quick):
- 2025-01-08: heuristic toggle merged to enable "align-to-preferred-window" by default (PR 893).
- 2025-01-09 09:12: repeated customer-reported throughput anomalies.
- 2025-01-09 10:00: temporary revert rolled for a single region; metric partial recovery.
- 2025-01-13: similar regression observed in a different region after canary of updated estimator.

What I ran (commands and queries I used during triage):
- kubectl tail logs (shortened):
  kubectl -n inference logs deploy/continuous-batcher -c batch-worker --since=2h | grep -i "window" | tail -n 200
- quick grep for alignment decisions (on a debug build):
  rg "align_to_preferred_window|estimator_decision" /var/log/ci-debug/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'
- PromQL samples:
  rate(serving_tokens_total[5m]) by (region)
  increase(kv_cache_hits_total[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total[10m])
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(serving_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,route))
- ad-hoc SQL against TSDB (clickhouse):
  select floor(toUnixTimestamp(ts)/60)*60 as minute, avg(tokens_per_sec) from metrics.serving where route = 'chat/v1' and ts > now() - interval 2 day group by minute order by minute desc limit 240
- Trace sampling examples: pulled spans where batch_size <= 4 and recorded warmup=false in the trace tags.

Representative log snippets (sanitized):
- "INFO aligner: preferred_window=16 estimated=8 decision=align_to_preferred_window=false reason=low_confidence_var(0.72)"
- "WARN batch-warmup: window_mismatch detected: requested_window=16 assigned_window=8 fill_ratio=0.28"
- "DEBUG kvcache: prefill_miss for request_id=... dropping prefix cache due to eviction_hint=true"

Hypotheses (ordered by plausibility):
1) Estimator misclassifies high-variance sequence distributions as "unstable" and forces smaller windows; smaller windows + high churn reduces KV-cache locality and reduces batching efficiency.
2) The alignment fallback logic accidentally prioritizes minimizing latency for short sequences at the cost of throughput when variance>threshold -> unlatching the preferred window too aggressively.
3) Race between metric-based autoscaler and window alignment: scaling decisions triggered more frequently when window sizes shrink, causing cold-start-like behavior.
4) A non-obvious interaction with route-level throttles: certain routes with tight per-route quotas are being assigned tiny windows to fit quota limits, exacerbating fragmentation.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses: (what I ran and what to run next)
- Reproduce locally with a mixed workload generator (short: seq_len~8, long: seq_len~512 at 1:20 ratio). Observed batch-size distribution shifts when toggling align_to_preferred_window flag.
- Toggle estimator to conservative-mode in canary and watch kv_cache_hit_rate and tokens/s. Did this for region-us-west1 and saw token throughput improve ~18% within 10 minutes. Suggests estimator tuning the culprit.
- Correlate autoscaler events (scale_up/scale_down) with window change events: query cluster events logs where timestamp within +- 1m of a window-size-change.
- Check per-route quota logs for assignments issued in same time range.

Config diffs worth examining (from PR 893):
- estimator: var_threshold default changed 0.6 -> 0.7
- fallback: allow_align_when_low_confidence = true (new)
- metric_window_seconds: 30 -> 10 (more reactive)
Potentially the shorter metric window makes estimator too jittery on mixed workloads.

Immediate mitigation options tried (and results):
- Rollback allow_align_when_low_confidence: quick revert on canary region improved throughput. (temporary, but confirms feature impact).
- Increase metric_window_seconds back to 30s in canary: smoother decisions, throughput improved, but latency for some short requests increased slightly.
- Add a short cooldown (30s) before changing window size per serving-worker to avoid flapping; needs more testing.

Open questions and next steps:
- Is the estimator variance calc biased by outliers? Maybe use trimmed-variance or median-absolute-deviation instead of sample variance.
- Should we treat routes with mixed sequence-length histograms specially (sticky preferred windows)?
- Can we add a microbenchmark to the PR that simulates mixed short/long distributions to catch regressions? (Yes — add to runtime unit/integration tests).
- Should KV-cache prefill logic be decoupled from immediate window decisions (prefill in background when possible)?

Notes to self / low-priority ideas:
- Add metric: batch_fill_ratio_by_window_size (helps quantify inefficiency).
- Add trace tag: chosen_window_reason (estimator|fallback|manual) to make triage faster.
- Consider smoothing estimator output with an EWMA to avoid aggressive toggles.

Slack links and pins (copied to ticket):
- #eng-runtime thread (Jan 9) -> slack://thread/CA12345/abcdef
- Quick repro script in gist: https://gist.github.com/priyash/1a2b3c (workload generator pattern included)

Action items (PRs/TODOs):
- short-term: revert allow_align_when_low_confidence in rollout branch and push cooldown gate (Priya, today)
- medium: add mixed-workload microbenchmark to CI, extend metric window to 30s or configurable (Liam)
- long-term: redesign estimator to use robust stats + add trace tags (Sofia + eng-serving-runtime)

If I don't follow up by EOD tomorrow: escalate to on-call and open INF-1427 with the revert patch details and metric snapshots.

Raw scratch commands (so I don't forget):
- kubectl -n inference port-forward svc/runtime-metrics 9091:9091 &
- curl -s http://localhost:9091/metrics | rg "kv_cache|batch_size|preferred_window" | less
- clickhouse-client --query "select toStartOfMinute(ts) as m, avg(tokens_per_sec) from metrics.serving where ts > now() - interval 3 day and region='us-west1' group by m order by m desc limit 120"
- rg "allow_align_when_low_confidence|metric_window_seconds" -n runtime/config

End of notes.

(keeping for personal record — will push a cleaned-up timeline into INF-1427 and add the repro script to the PR comments)
